outcomes.original: Estimated time: 240 to 540 days. Estimated government cost: $8,500 to $24,000. Notes: The critical path is the Conditional Use Authorization (120–300 days, $3,100–$15,000 per catalog:sf.conditional_use_authorization) followed by the ABC Type 42 license transfer (60–150 days, $1,000–$1,600 per catalog:ca.abc_type_42). The Mission SUD license-transfer requirement adds 1–3 months to locate and escrow a qualifying license, and the undue-concentration flag may trigger a Public Convenience or Necessity process adding another 60–90 days. The Place of Entertainment permit (45–120 days, $2,708–$3,800 per catalog:sf.place_of_entertainment_permit) can run in parallel with the building permit (14–120 days, $800–$15,000 per catalog:sf.building_permit) after CUA approval. Health plan check and permit add 35–105 days and $1,298–$3,500 (catalog:sf.health_plan_check, catalog:sf.health_permit). Minor costs include business registration ($55–$700), sign permit ($300–$1,500), entity formation ($70–$150), food safety certifications ($100–$250), RBS training ($3–$30 per employee) and music licenses ($600–$5,000 annually). The timeline assumes no significant delays from neighbor appeals, incomplete plans or failed inspections. Budget 8–18 months from lease signature to opening, with government fees of $8,500–$24,000 not including construction, rent, insurance, legal or the license purchase price.
